nodes.name: Iron dip coating and drying
nodes.procedure: A piece of CF (1 × 2 cm²) was washed with DI water and dried under N₂. For the iron treatment, 0.25 M FeCl₃ solution was deposited on the porous CF by a dip coating process by soaking the CF (Fig. 1b) for 30 s and then dried using a convection oven at 70 °C for 1 h (denoted as CF-Fe). The Fe treatment (CF-Fe) led to corrosion and cracks on the CF owing to Cl ion (Fig. 1c).

nodes.name: Sulfurization heat treatment
nodes.procedure: The prepared CF-Fe electrode was sulfurized by heat treatment with sulfur. Sulfur powder (200 mg) and Fe-CF were put into each side of a quartz boat. The quartz boat with sulfur powder and Fe-CF was put into the center of a furnace tube. The side of the quartz boat with CF was placed downstream of the furnace. The furnace temperature was raised to 300 °C (at 10 °C/min,) and maintained for 5 min. The furnace was cooled down to room temperature (denoted as CF-FeS).
nodes.source_text: The prepared CF-Fe electrode was sulfurized by heat treatment with sulfur... The furnace temperature was raised to 300 °C (at 10 °C/min,) and maintained for 5 min.

nodes.name: Electrochemical reconstruction under OER conditions
nodes.procedure: The electrochemical reconstruction process was conducted in a three-electrode system with iron and sulfur-treated CF (denoted as CF-FeS) as the working electrode, graphite electrode as the counter electrode, and Hg/HgO as the reference electrode in O₂-saturated 1 M KOH electrolyte. For electrochemical reconstruction process, a current density of 100 mA cm⁻² was applied for 10 min. To check the completion of electrochemical reconstruction, cyclic voltammetry was performed in the potential range 1–1.8 V vs RHE at 100 mV s⁻¹ for 50 cycles, 10 mV s⁻¹ for 10 cycles, and 2 mV s⁻¹ for 2 cycles. If the electrochemical reconstruction process is not completed, the CV will appear slanted. After the electrochemical reconstruction, the iron and sulfur-treated CF (CF-FeSO) was washed with DI water. The S and remaining Cl⁻ species were dissolved and exchanged with oxygen species (O²⁻, OH⁻), thereby reconstructing the highly rough structure with abundant Fe-doped Co nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: CF-FeSO possesses abundant nanosheet structures on the highly rough surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images in Fig. 1e and Supplementary Fig. 6 revealed that CF-FeSO possesses abundant nanosheet structures on the highly rough surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images of CF-FeSO showed the formation of thin nanosheets with an oxidized structure on the CF surface, such as layered double hydroxide structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of CF-FeSO showed the formation of thin nanosheets with an oxidized structure on the CF surface, such as layered double hydroxide structure (Fig. 1f, g).

nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) of the TEM and SEM images reveals the homogenous incorporation of Fe on the CF despite the rough dip coating process.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co L-edge NEXAFS shows CF-FeSO has Co³⁺(O_h):Co²⁺(T_d) ratio of 2.32:1 indicating mixture of CoOOH and Co₃O₄; CF-SO has ratio 1.56:1 between CoO and Co₃O₄; CF-O shows Co²⁺(T_d) and Co²⁺(O_h) with 3d⁷ configuration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co L-edge of CF-O exhibits peaks corresponding to Co²⁺(T_d) and Co²⁺(O_h) with the 3d⁷ configuration... The ratio of Co³⁺(O_h) and Co²⁺(T_d) is 1.56:1... The ratio of Co³⁺(O_h) and Co²⁺(T_d) was 2.32:1, indicating that CF-FeSO is a mixture of CoOOH and Co₃O₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: O K-edge NEXAFS of CF-FeSO shows only eg orbital peaks, suggesting completely filled t2g orbitals and LS (t2g⁶ eg⁰) state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The only eg orbital peaks of CF-FeSO were observed in the O K-edge, suggesting completely filled t2g orbitals.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectrum of CF-FeSO shows two peaks corresponding to Eg of CoOOH and A1g of Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two peaks, corresponding to Eg of CoOOH and A1g of Co₃O₄, were observed in the spectrum of CF-FeSO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows CF-SO peaked at 7725 eV with higher intensity than CF-O, indicating higher Co oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spectrum of CF-SO peaked at 7725 eV and was more intense and higher than that of CF-O.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at different scan rates shows CF-FeSO has higher internal and external voltammetric charge densities than CF-SO and CF-O, indicating S treatment significantly increased electrode roughness and produced abundant active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results of calculated charge density and electrochemical porosity suggested that S treatment not only significantly increased the electrode roughness, but also produced abundant catalytically active sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman of CF-FeSO shows only CoOOH (Eg) peak retained up to 1.53 V, demonstrating Fe-CoOOH is the main active site.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Even if the applied potential for the case of CF-FeSO increases to 1.53 V, only the CoOOH peak is detected, demonstrating that Fe-CoOOH is the main active site for the OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Co K-edge XANES shows CF-FeSO maintained stable oxidation states of Co³⁺ and Fe³⁺ from OCV up to 1.63 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CF-FeSO showed stable oxidation states of Co³⁺ and Fe³⁺ from OCV up to 1.63 V, confirming that the Fe-doped CoOOH sites maintained stable phases under harsh OER condition.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Co L-edge NEXAFS of CP-FeSO shows high proportion of Co³⁺ state (Fe-CoOOH) under OER with small t2g peak indicating transformation to intermediate spin (IS, t2g⁵ eg¹) state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At 1.43 V, the Co L-edge of CP-FeSO almost maintained the position of the main peaks with decreasing Co²⁺ species, indicating a high proportion of the Co³⁺ state (Fe-CoOOH)... This suggested that Fe-CoOOH in CP-FeSO transformed to an intermediate spin (IS, t2g⁵ eg¹) state from the LS state during the OER.

nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectrum suggested that Co and S were present at an atomic ratio of 1:1.74.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns and TEM images of CP-FeSO indicate well reconstructed structure.
